A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same parameter-free Sign-SGD research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching SOS and toy experiments across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LIBSVM experiments, 130M LLaMA pre-training results on C4, and Swin fine-tuning results on TinyImageNet.

after.justification: v4 retains these results and reports additional memory-variant, robustness, 350M LLaMA, MRI reconstruction, and molecular-property experiments. Appendix A.3 distinguishes its original ALIAS results from externally attributed baseline scores.

M1.justification: v4 Section 3.3 introduces a memory-efficient ALIAS variant absent from v2. It exchanges the norms in the local smoothness estimator and approximates gradient differences using coordinate extrema, retaining previous gradient signs and two scalars instead of the full previous gradient. The existing SOS, ALIAS, and momentum approaches remain.

E1.justification: v4 Appendix A.3 adds fastMRI reconstruction and OGBG molecular-property prediction, substantially extending the evaluated domains and tasks. C4 pre-training, TinyImageNet fine-tuning, and the four LIBSVM datasets remain; the convex and non-convex toy experiments move to Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: v4 Table 7 adds evaluated DoG, D-Adaptation with Adam, and MoMo with Adam to the LLaMA parameter-free comparisons, extending v2's comparison with Prodigy. The original language and vision comparator sets remain. Table 11 additionally compares against explicitly attributed baseline results for the new tasks.

E3.justification: v4 introduces a 350M LLaMA configuration, batch-size comparisons using 512, 256, 128, and 64 sequences, and an initial-value comparison using d0 = 1 and 0.001. New U-Net and GNN evaluations use SSIM and mAP. The existing 130M training setup and 50-epoch Swin protocol are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds exact-versus-approximated norm ablations for the memory-efficient variant, initialization sensitivity, and batch-size experiments intended to test gradient-noise robustness. These investigate substantial new questions beyond v2's stepsize dynamics and L-infinity sensitivity analysis, which remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. The shaded region in v4 Figure 3 displays the gap between exact and approximated norms, without introducing repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original 130M results in Tables 1–2 and Swin accuracies remain unchanged. v4 adds memory-variant, robustness, and additional-baseline results, plus a 350M ALIAS Adam loss of 2.707 and MRI/MPP scores of 0.724 SSIM and 0.242 mAP. Table 11 reports AdamW at 0.254 mAP, so the new findings do not establish superiority over AdamW on both tasks.

T1.justification: v4 adds L1-smoothness Assumption 3.11, Theorem 3.12, and Appendix F.4's descent lemma and convergence proof for the norm-modified ALIAS variant, including dimension-dependent bounds. Existing SOS, ALIAS, and steepest-descent analyses are substantially retained. The new guarantee explicitly covers the exact norm formulation, not its practical extrema approximation.

C1.justification: v4 elevates memory-efficient adaptive optimization to a main contribution and adds an approximately 1.5-fold end-to-end speedup claim in the abstract. Its contribution narrative centers ALIAS, whereas v2 foregrounds SOS and ALIAS together. The underlying parameter-free, stochastic, distributed, and momentum claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses ALIAS's full-gradient storage requirement, the memory variant's theoretical boundaries, and its accuracy tradeoff. Appendix A.1.2 explains how norm overestimation produces smaller steps and interprets initialization and noise sensitivity. Section 3 also adds a substantive justification for using convex theory to inform neural-network optimization.

D1.justification: v4 adds explicit stochastic pseudocode distinguishing the practical and theoretical options and documenting shared-sample gradient calculations. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named ALIAS repository link and revises the LLaMA compute description to four A100 GPUs and approximately 12 hours. Most previously reported training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 makes focused additions covering recent Sign-SGD momentum, heavy-tailed-noise and privacy research, convexity-related neural-network work, and MoMo/AlgoPerf. It removes several broad LLM-background references. The central positioning around unknown stepsize quantities and much of the parameter-free optimization review remain.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the title, extensively rewrites the abstract and introductory narrative, and reorganizes the presentation around ALIAS. SOS and its toy experiments move to Appendix B, while the experimental appendix gains a clearer study-by-study structure. A conclusion and additional explanatory passages are added.

P2.justification: v4 replaces v2's pervasive boxed presentation with a conference layout, places Tables 1–2 side by side, and moves the retained LLaMA training curves into the main text. It adds norm-approximation and 350M figures and several new tables, revises highlighting and captions, and relocates the toy plots. Table 1 also corrects the first baseline label to match the already-described constant learning rate.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v2's tension between its memory-efficiency motivation and ALIAS's full-gradient storage: the new variant reports 0.41 GB versus 1.22 GB, with validation loss increasing modestly from 3.006 to 3.019. Broader parameter-free comparisons, larger-model and cross-domain evaluations, and targeted ablations materially strengthen validation. These gains outweigh the accuracy tradeoff, although the practical approximation remains outside the proved guarantee and the new 1.5-fold speedup claim lacks a corresponding end-to-end timing comparison.
